articles.title: Building a Fully Automated CI/CD Pipeline on AWS with Docker, ECR, CodeBuild, CodePipeline and ECS Fargate
articles.excerpt: Introduction Shipping software by hand is one of the quickest ways to introduce mistakes. Someone builds an image on their laptop, pushes it to a registry, logs into a console and clicks through a dep…
articles.body: Introduction Shipping software by hand is one of the quickest ways to introduce mistakes. Someone builds an image on their laptop, pushes it to a registry, logs into a console and clicks through a deployment. It works until the day a step is skipped, a wrong tag is deployed or the one person who knows the process is on leave. Continuous Integration and Continuous Delivery (CI/CD) solves this by turning the release process into code that runs the same way every time. In this project I built a complete CI/CD pipeline on AWS that takes a change from a git push to a running container on Amazon ECS Fargate , with no manual steps in between. To keep the focus on the pipeline rather than the application, I used the classic 2048 game as the workload.
articles.author: Shehzad Ahmad

articles.title: Aligning Development Speed with Security Controls to Prevent Weekend Incident Burnout
articles.excerpt: The Friday 5:00 PM Breach: Anatomy of an After-Hours Incident At 4:58 PM on a Friday, the pager does not merely emit an audio tone; it triggers a sympathetic nervous system cascade inside the on-call…
articles.body: The Friday 5:00 PM Breach: Anatomy of an After-Hours Incident At 4:58 PM on a Friday, the pager does not merely emit an audio tone; it triggers a sympathetic nervous system cascade inside the on-call engineer. Epinephrine floods the bloodstream, heart rate spikes, and forty-eight hours of planned recovery—whether a quiet evening finally booting up Grand Theft Auto VI or dinner with family—evaporate instantly. The incident queue lights up because an upstream builder pushed an unvetted system into production immediately before logging off for the weekend. Forensic reconstruction of these late-week compromises shows that root causes rarely involve zero-day exploits.
articles.author: Olga Larionova

articles.title: How to learn maths and CS with AI without fooling yourself
articles.excerpt: If you're using AI to learn a hard maths or CS topic, I'd stop asking it for tutorials. A generated tutorial reads smoothly and you come away feeling you've understood it, but you haven't done anythin…
articles.body: If you're using AI to learn a hard maths or CS topic, I'd stop asking it for tutorials. A generated tutorial reads smoothly and you come away feeling you've understood it, but you haven't done anything yet, and doing it is the part that makes it stick. What has worked better for me and for the people I teach is keeping a proper textbook or set of lecture notes as the spine. Somebody who knows the subject has already decided the order things come in and which examples matter. The AI then gets two narrower jobs. Job one: problems, and finding your first mistake Once you've read a section, ask for five exercises on it that go from routine to hard, without the answers, and do them on paper. Then paste your attempt and ask where the first mistake is.

articles.title: Silent CPU Fallback in Ollama: How to Detect and Prevent CUDA Spillover
articles.excerpt: You pull a 14B or 32B model in Ollama. On the first prompt, response generation is blazing fast—delivering a smooth 35 to 45 tokens per second. But on your third turn, after feeding in a 3,000-token f…
articles.body: You pull a 14B or 32B model in Ollama. On the first prompt, response generation is blazing fast—delivering a smooth 35 to 45 tokens per second. But on your third turn, after feeding in a 3,000-token function definition or log trace, generation suddenly grinds to a halt. The model stutters, your CPU fans rev to 100%, and token generation plummets to a painful 1.2 tokens per second . Your GPU has not crashed, and Ollama hasn't thrown an error. What you are witnessing is silent CPU fallback —one of the most frustrating performance traps in local AI engineering.

articles.title: Page Likes vs Post Likes: Rank Your Facebook Posts by Real Engagement With Python (Bangladesh Edition)
articles.excerpt: By MD Fozla Rabbi, SEO Specialist Here's a question I hear from Facebook sellers in Dhaka all the time. "My page has 18,000 likes. Why do my posts get 40 reactions?" Short answer: page likes and post…
articles.body: By MD Fozla Rabbi , SEO Specialist Here's a question I hear from Facebook sellers in Dhaka all the time. "My page has 18,000 likes. Why do my posts get 40 reactions?" Short answer: page likes and post likes are two very different things. Page likes are a lifetime number. Post likes are what happens today, to this one post, with this one audience. Most small sellers only watch the first number. It's big and it only goes up. Comfortable. But the second number is where sales actually start. So I wrote a short Python script that reads a Facebook post export and ranks every post by real engagement. It tells you which posts people actually responded to, which ones flopped and what time of day works best for your page. Standard library only. Runs on any laptop.

articles.title: A Tiny UTM Link Builder in Plain JavaScript for Filipino Shops Selling on Facebook and TikTok
articles.excerpt: By MD Fozla Rabbi, SEO Specialist A friend runs a small milk tea shop in Quezon City. She sells on Facebook, TikTok and a little on Instagram. Orders come through a simple order page on her site. Last…
articles.body: By MD Fozla Rabbi , SEO Specialist A friend runs a small milk tea shop in Quezon City. She sells on Facebook, TikTok and a little on Instagram. Orders come through a simple order page on her site. Last month she asked me a fair question. "Which app actually brings the orders?" I opened her analytics. Almost everything said direct or (not set) . No idea where people came from. Her links in bios and captions were just bare URLs. The fix is boring and old: UTM parameters. Tiny tags at the end of a link that tell your analytics where a click came from. The problem is nobody types them right by hand. One post says facebook , the next says FB , the next says Facebook with a trailing space. Now you've got three sources that are really one.

articles.excerpt: With the release of Meta's Llama 3.3 70B Instruct, developers finally have an open-weight model that rivals closed frontier models like Claude 3.5 Sonnet and GPT-4o on coding and reasoning benchmarks.…
articles.body: With the release of Meta's Llama 3.3 70B Instruct , developers finally have an open-weight model that rivals closed frontier models like Claude 3.5 Sonnet and GPT-4o on coding and reasoning benchmarks. However, the immediate question every local AI practitioner faces is: Can I actually run a 70-billion-parameter model on consumer hardware, or is it strictly reserved for $10,000 dual-A100 server clusters? The short answer is yes —consumer workstations with 24GB VRAM (like an RTX 3090, RTX 4090, or Apple Silicon M-series Mac) can run Llama 3.3 70B smoothly, provided you master the exact physics of tensor quantization, KV-cache allocation, and context memory scaling .

articles.title: On this day in space! Nov. 20, 1998:  Russia launches 1st module of International Space Station as construction begins on the largest human-built structure in orbit
articles.excerpt: On Nov. 20, 1998, the first piece of the International Space Station launched into orbit. It was just one piece, but the foundation of something much larger.
articles.body: On Nov. 20, 1998, the first piece of the International Space Station launched into orbit. The 42,000-pound module is called Zarya, and it's about the size of a tour bus. Zarya launched on board a Russian Proton rocket . Two weeks later, NASA's STS-88 shuttle mission aboard Endeavour brought the Unity module into space. The STS-88 astronauts connected the two modules in orbit. Zarya was built by the Russians, but it was paid for by the United States. NASA contracted a Russian company to build it for half the price of what the American company Lockheed Martin would have charged. These days, Zarya is mainly used for storage and for external fuel tanks. The module also has docking ports for Russian Progress cargo ships and Soyuz spacecraft that carry crews to and from the space station.

articles.body: Researchers are calling for a moratorium on industrial exploitation of the moon, fearing that rapid development could cause irreversible environmental damage and destroy invaluable scientific material. Both China and the U.S. are pushing forward with plans to establish permanent human settlements on the moon by the end of the next decade. Commercial players want to build businesses supporting these future explorers by mining for resources such as water , construction materials, industrial metals and rare earth minerals. However, some scientists argue that a temporary ban on lunar industrialization is necessary to allow regulations to catch up and limit what can be allowed in order to prevent a moon rush from destroying the pristine lunar environment.
